costNodePlain: Money set aside for loans that may not be repaid — the provision for credit losses: $1,956M of loans were charged off in the quarter, partly offset by a $72M net reserve release (a $142M net release in Wholesale, partly offset by a $44M net build in Consumer and other items), leaving a provision of $1,884M.

opex.name: Compensation expense
opex.note: Pay and benefits for the bank's workforce — its biggest cost, up 12% on more employees and higher pay, including staff added with First Republic.

opex.name: Professional & outside services
opex.note: Professional fees and outside services combined, as reported in the supplement — up 4%.

opex.name: Technology, communications & equipment
opex.note: Technology, communications and equipment — up 11% as the bank keeps investing in its platforms.

opex.name: Occupancy & other expense
opex.note: Branches and offices ($1,211M of occupancy) plus other expense ($2,299M) — other expense jumped 40%, driven by the $725M increase to the FDIC special assessment in Corporate.

footerNote: JPMorgan headlines 'managed' revenue of $42.5B; this page uses reported (GAAP) revenue of $41.9B — the $614M difference is a fully taxable-equivalent gross-up of tax-exempt income ($121M in net interest income and $493M in noninterest revenue) that does not change net income. For a bank, credit costs (the provision for credit losses) play the role of cost of revenue, and operating profit here is income before income taxes.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: reported basis, vs a year ago

oneTimers: $725M increase to the estimated FDIC special assessment in Corporate — the release's flagged 'significant item' for 1Q24, reflecting the FDIC's revised estimated losses to the Deposit Insurance Fund from the 2023 bank failures. It reduced EPS by $0.19; excluding it, net income was $14.0B ($4.63 per share) instead of $13.4B ($4.44). It sits inside other expense, in the 'Occupancy & other expense' bucket on this page.
$366M of net investment securities losses in Corporate, predominantly from sales of mortgage-backed securities and U.S. Treasuries (versus $868M of net securities losses in 1Q23).

First Republic (acquired May 1, 2023) contributed $668M of net income in the quarter — $1.3B of net interest income and $315M of noninterest revenue, less $806M of expense and a $31M net benefit to the provision — per the release; it is included in all reported figures above, not stripped out.

segments.name: Net interest income
segments.note: Interest earned on loans and securities, minus the interest paid on deposits and borrowings — the bank's core engine, up 11% on balance-sheet mix, higher rates and higher revolving Card Services balances (and the First Republic portfolio), partly offset by deposit margin compression and lower deposit balances in Consumer & Community Banking.

segments.name: Noninterest revenue
segments.note: Fees, trading and asset-management income — up 7% on higher asset management fees and higher Investment Banking fees, partly offset by lower Markets revenue; Corporate also booked $366M of net investment securities losses, versus $868M of losses a year ago.

takeaways.text: Reported net interest income rose 11% to $23.1B — 55% of all revenue — on balance-sheet mix, higher rates and higher revolving card balances, even as deposit margins compressed in the consumer bank.
takeaways.title: Interest income did the heavy lifting

takeaways.text: A $725M increase to the FDIC special assessment (in Corporate, inside other expense) cut EPS by $0.19. Excluding it, net income was $14.0B, or $4.63 per share, instead of $13.4B and $4.44.
takeaways.title: One charge hid $0.6B of profit

takeaways.text: The provision dropped 17% to $1.9B: $2.0B of net charge-offs — mostly normalising Card Services losses — were partly offset by a $72M net reserve release, versus a $1.1B reserve build a year ago.
takeaways.title: Credit costs fell year on year

verdict: JPMorgan made $13.4B as reported revenue rose 9% to $41.9B — and profit would have been $14.0B without a $725M extra FDIC charge tied to last year's bank failures.
